description:
DeriveCallGraphComponent walks every function reachable from its subject (collect_static_graph, keying.rs ~1018; strong_component keying.rs:1050-1067), so a program pays a whole reachable walk per function: quadratic. Measured on Enum.take on fz-afu.2: 48 runs, 520 StaticCallees reads, max 51 in one run (main/0 50, Enum.take/2 49). Chain case (h<-g<-f<-main): per-run reads main [1,2,3,4], f 3, g 2, h 1.

Refuted (fz-afu.3 reader, 2026-09-26): stopping the walk at a callee whose component is already known. Saves 472 -> 451 reads on Enum.take and none on the chain, because callers run before callees; it cannot wait instead (f waits on g while g waits on f); and it is unsound when StaticCallees grows later (lambda targets / provider boundary, keying.rs:69-72, 106-133): if B later gains B -> C -> A with {A} already published, B's walk stops at A and never reads A -> B.

Shapes to weigh on a page (needs the proposal method before any build):
- one walk per root that finds every group at once, as annotate_back_edges (native.rs:4339-4387) does once per module; needs an answer for who publishes each function's CallGraphComponent and how a grown edge set re-opens it.
- waits that follow call edges, a wait cycle read as a recursive group; puts cycle detection in the scheduler.
The same shape appears in statically_reaches (transport.rs:2223-2245), on a rare path; the page says whether it folds into the same answer.

Acceptance: CallGraphComponent reads proportional to edges (not edges x functions) on Enum.take, pinned; Recursive answers unchanged on every fixture; a test where StaticCallees grows to close a new cycle.
title: The recursive-group question costs one walk per program, not one per function
